correctness.rationale: For all positive m,b, F^4=(h^2,h^2) with increasing bounded h^2; the algebraic two-cycle relation forces m>1. Hyperbolic parametrization b=B_m(s), strict increase from the convexity of t coth t, and limiting endpoints prove uniqueness and the sharp threshold. Exact scalar multipliers establish the three-root global basins and both primitive four-cycle types. At the neutral boundary, the explicitly derived cubic term -(m^2-1)/6 in g^2 yields the signed inverse-square law, and four differentiable compositions give the four-phase vector limit. Recurrent-point support gives the invariant/physical measures. Exact rational and independent finite checks ran successfully in verification.py; finite experiments are not the proof. No claim about finite-tau maps.

value.rationale: The singular map and its two observed four-cycles are naturally motivated by the original modeling paper, but a complete global all-parameter phase portrait was not provided there. The present threshold exactly separates one ergodic probability from three, with sharply specified full-measure basins and exceptional saddle axes. At the neutral 1:4 boundary, global convergence persists and has a parameter-explicit four-phase n^-1/2 law that distinguishes all coordinate quadrants; this is structurally meaningful for critical relaxation and physical observation rather than an arbitrary finite example. The hyperbolic uniqueness argument supplies nontrivial mathematical work, and no general theorem is falsely claimed beyond this family.
